title: Queens Hazard Ranking
Queens Hazard Ranking
text:
Heavy Rain
The impact of heavy rain on a given Community District is taken as the percent area that experiences stormwater flooding of any kind (i.e. greater than 4 inches of flooding without sea level rise under a limited- or moderate-intensity rainfall event)2. Citywide, this percentage ranges from 0.3% to 3.52%. In Queens, the percentage ranges from 0.41% to 3.08%. All 59 Community Districts experience some stormwater flooding.


Code
boro_fill <- list(
  scale_fill_manual(
    name   = NULL,
    values = c(`TRUE` = "#3258a3", `FALSE` = "#cedef0"),
    labels = c(`TRUE` = "Queens", `FALSE` = "Other Boroughs"),
    breaks = c(TRUE, FALSE)
  ),
  theme(
    legend.position      = "top",
    legend.justification = "left",
    legend.margin        = margin(t = 0, b = 6),
    legend.key.size      = unit(11, "pt"),
    legend.text          = element_text(size = 9)
  )
)

ggplot(cdta) + 
  geom_col(aes(x = fct_reorder(CDTA2020, stormwater_pct), 
               y = stormwater_pct,
               fill = BoroCode == 4)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = median(cdta$stormwater_pct),
             linetype = "dashed", colour = "#ea4943") +
  theme(
    panel.background   = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor.y = element_line(colour = "#ebebeb"),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "#ebebeb"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5)
    )+
  labs(title = "Stormwater Flood Extent in CDTAs", x = "CDTA", y = "Stormwater Flood Extent [%]") +
  annotate("text", x = 1, y = median(cdta$stormwater_pct),
           label = "Citywide median", colour = "#ea4943",
           hjust = 0, vjust = -0.6, size = 3) +
  boro_fill

title: Queens Hazard Ranking
text:
Coastal Storm
The Department of Health and Mental Hygiene’s Flood Vulnerability Index estimates neighborhood vulnerability to flooding by combining susceptibility to harm and capacity to recover3. This project makes use of the storm surge index based on current-current day sea level. CDTAs are assigned an FVI value of 1-5 based on the maximum census tract value that overlaps with the district boundary. Based on this approach, 40 of 59 NYC CDTAs are vulnerable to coastal flooding; 9 of 14 Queens CDTAs are vulnerable to coastal flooding:


Code
cil_table(cdta |> 
            st_drop_geometry() |> 
            filter(BoroCode == 4) |> 
            select(CDTAName, max_ss_cur_fvi) |> 
            mutate(max_ss_cur_fvi = as.character(max_ss_cur_fvi)) |> 
            rename(
              "CDTA Name" = "CDTAName",
              "Storm Surge FVI, 2020s" = "max_ss_cur_fvi"
            ),
          full_height = TRUE
          )

Code
ggplot(cdta) + 
  geom_col(aes(x = fct_reorder(CDTA2020, max_ss_cur_fvi, .na_rm = F, .default = -Inf), 
               y = max_ss_cur_fvi,
               fill = BoroCode == 4)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = median(cdta$max_ss_cur_fvi, na.rm = T),
             linetype = "dashed", colour = "#ea4943") +
  theme(
    panel.background   = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor.y = element_line(colour = "#ebebeb"),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "#ebebeb"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5)
    )+
  labs(title = "Flood Vulnerability Index in CDTAs",
       subtitle = "Storm Surge, 2020s Sea Level",
       x = "CDTA", y = "FVI [1-5]") +
  annotate("text", x = 1, y = median(cdta$max_ss_cur_fvi, na.rm = T),
           label = "Citywide median", colour = "#ea4943",
           hjust = 0, vjust = -0.6, size = 3) +
  boro_fill

title: Queens Hazard Ranking
text:
Extreme Heat
Similarly, DOHMH’s Heat Vulnerability Index combines neighborhood environmental and social factors to detail the distribution of the risk of death from heat4. Unlike the FVI, the HVI is released at the CDTA level, so aggregation is not necessary.


Code
ggplot(cdta) + 
  geom_col(aes(x = fct_reorder(CDTA2020, HVI), 
               y = HVI,
               fill = BoroCode == 4)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = median(cdta$HVI),
             linetype = "dashed", colour = "#ea4943") +
  theme(
    panel.background   = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor.y = element_line(colour = "#ebebeb"),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "#ebebeb"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5)
    )+
  labs(title = "Heat Vulnerability Index in CDTAs", x = "CDTA", y = "HVI [1-5]") +
  annotate("text", x = 1, y = median(cdta$HVI),
           label = "Citywide median", colour = "#ea4943",
           hjust = 0, vjust = -0.6, size = 3) +
  boro_fill

title: Queens Hazard Ranking
text:
Hazmat / Chemical
Two hazmat / chemical threat data sources are referenced in the 2024 JRA report.
The first is a dataset of Chemically Intensive Small Businesses, which provides a count of these businesses per CDTA5. The count ranges from 4 to 202 citywide; In Queens, the range is from 25 to 202. Notably, 10 of 14 Queens CDTAs have more chemically intensive small businesses than the citywide median. The CDTA with the highest number of chemically intensive small businesses is Astoria-Queensbridge.


Code
ggplot(cdta) + 
  geom_col(aes(x = fct_reorder(CDTA2020, chem_count), 
               y = chem_count,
               fill = BoroCode == 4)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = median(cdta$chem_count),
             linetype = "dashed", colour = "#ea4943") +
  theme(
    panel.background   = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor.y = element_line(colour = "#ebebeb"),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "#ebebeb"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5)
    )+
  labs(title = "Chemically Intensive Small Businesses in CDTAs", x = "CDTA", y = "Count") +
  annotate("text", x = 1, y = median(cdta$chem_count),
           label = "Citywide median", colour = "#ea4943",
           hjust = 0, vjust = -0.6, size = 3) +
  boro_fill









The second dataset contains the locations of Fuel Oil / Hazardous Waste Material Storage sites across the city6. These data come from the EPA’s Resource Conservation and Recovery Act biennial report. There are 207 sites citywide.Counting sites per district gives a range of 0 to 13; in Queens the range is 0 to 8. Sites are mapped below:


Code
# Compute quintiles for choropleth map
hazmat_breaks <- quantile(cdta$hazmat_count, probs = seq(0, 1, 0.2), type = 1)
hazmat_colors <- colorRampPalette(c("grey80", "#efd1cc", "#db7a6b", "#a44132"))(5)

# Bin labels based on breaks
bin_low  <- c(min(cdta$hazmat_count), unname(hazmat_breaks[2:5]))
bin_high <- c(unname(hazmat_breaks[2:5]) - 1, max(cdta$hazmat_count))
bin_labels <- ifelse(bin_low == bin_high, bin_low, paste0(bin_low, "–", bin_high))

# HTML popups
hazmat_sites <- hazmat_storage |>
  mutate(hazmat_popup = paste0("<strong>", HANDLER_NA, "</strong><br/>", TOP3))

maplibre(bounds = cdta,
         style = carto_style("positron")) |>
  add_fill_layer(
    id = "hazmat-count",
    source = cdta,
    fill_color = step_expr(
      column = "hazmat_count",
      base   = hazmat_colors[1],
      values = unname(hazmat_breaks[2:5]),
      stops  = hazmat_colors[-1]
    ),
    fill_opacity = 0.85,
    fill_outline_color = "#ffffff",
    popup = "CDTAName"
  ) |>
  add_circle_layer(
    id = "hazmat-sites",
    source = hazmat_sites,
    circle_color = "#0b0b0b",
    circle_radius = 4,
    circle_stroke_color = "#ffffff",
    circle_stroke_width = 1,
    popup = "hazmat_popup"
  ) |>
  add_legend(
    "Hazmat sites per CDTA",
    values = bin_labels,
    colors = hazmat_colors,
    type = "categorical",
    style = list(
      background_color = "#fefcfa",
      backgroud_opacity = 0.8
    )
  )






Hazmat location count by CDTA:


Code
ggplot(cdta) + 
  geom_col(aes(x = fct_reorder(CDTA2020, hazmat_count), 
               y = hazmat_count,
               fill = BoroCode == 4)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = median(cdta$hazmat_count),
             linetype = "dashed", colour = "#ea4943") +
  theme(
    panel.background   = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor.y = element_line(colour = "#ebebeb"),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "#ebebeb"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5)
    )+
  labs(title = "Hazmat storage locations in CDTAs", x = "CDTA", y = "Count") +
  annotate("text", x = 1, y = median(cdta$hazmat_count),
           label = "Citywide median", colour = "#ea4943",
           hjust = 0, vjust = -0.6, size = 3) + 
  boro_fill

title: Queens Hazard Ranking
text:
Infectious Disease
The 2024 JRA also references DOHMH’s Pandemic Influenza Vulnerability Index, is produced by analyzing potential exposure, susceptibility, and access to treatment at the Community District Level7. Note that Queens CDTAs have PIVI values of 1 or 2 (out of 5):


Code
ggplot(cdta) + 
  geom_col(aes(x = fct_reorder(CDTA2020, PIVI), 
               y = PIVI,
               fill = BoroCode == 4)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = median(cdta$PIVI),
             linetype = "dashed", colour = "#ea4943") +
  theme(
    panel.background   = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor.y = element_line(colour = "#ebebeb"),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "#ebebeb"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5)
    )+
  labs(title = "Pandemic Influenza Vulnerability Index in CDTAs", x = "CDTA", y = "Count") +
  annotate("text", x = 1, y = median(cdta$PIVI),
           label = "Citywide median", colour = "#ea4943",
           hjust = 0, vjust = -0.6, size = 3) +
  boro_fill

title: What’s changed
text:
BetaNYC

This page lists the changes to the Queens Hazard Ranking report that a reader would notice, newest first, including corrections when we published something wrong.
History begins: 2026-09-08, the day the report was first published. Dates are the day each version went up on the site, in New York time. Corrections made before this date may be missing.Data refresh: none. The figures come from NYC Open Data and City reports as they stood when the report was last built, and they do not update on their own.
To report a bug in the report, or to ask for a new feature, open an issue on GitHub.

A first ranking of hazards for each Queens district
September 10, 2026
Tags: Site, Data
The report now scores five hazards from 1 to 5 for each Queens district (Community District Tabulation Area) and puts them in order, with a map or chart for each hazard. Heavy rain and hazmat are now scored in fifths, replacing the first version's table of citywide percentiles for stormwater flooding. The report calls this an initial ranking and says the remaining hazards would be placed using feedback from subject matter experts.
More detail: The commit · Same-day edits
Link to this change: A first ranking of hazards for each Queens district


The report is published
September 8, 2026
Tags: Site, Data
The first version regroups the ten hazards in the City's 2024 Jurisdictional Risk Assessment into eight hazards for the Queens Resource Map, lists the data available to compare Queens districts on each one, and shows how much of each district floods in heavy rain.
